heard: Ranger Ed Pulaski saved 40 men by holding them at gunpoint. In 1910, hurricane winds whipped Idaho into a three-million-acre firestorm. Smoke-blinded ships in the Pacific and turned midday into night. Trapped, Pulaski forced his panic crew into an abandoned mine tunnel. He drew his pistol to prevent them from fleeing into the flames. Wildland firefighters still carry the tool named for the ranger who saved 40 men.
